WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of her

From the textEsther was queen as the king's wife, not as a reigning monarch: he "made her queen instead of Vashti", and the decrees went out "in the king’s name", sealed with his ring. Esther 2:17 Esther 8:8–10
Mordecai to Esther: "who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?" Esther 4:14
"And so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish." Esther 4:16
"Let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request." Esther 7:3

"Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote with all authority, to confirm this second letter of Purim"; "the decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim; and it was written in the book." Esther 9:29 Esther 9:32
HER PEOPLE
God's people in her time
The Jews fasted with her before she went to the king. Esther 4:16
Purim was confirmed by her decree "and it was written in the book". Esther 9:31–32
"The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour"; many of the people of the land "became Jews". Esther 8:16–17
The Jews "stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies" on the thirteenth of Adar. Esther 9:16–17
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
Each mark sits at the year of the reign the Bible gives for it.
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
Made queen in the tenth month of the king's seventh year (Esth 2:16).
IF AHASUERUS IS XERXES I: HIS SEVENTH YEAR, 479/478 BC
The tenth month, Tebeth, would fall about the turn of 479/478 BC on Parker and Dubberstein's tables; the identification is a view.
Amestris, Xerxes' queen in Herodotus
R. Dick Wilson (1915), as a possibility

Wilson suggests that if "Esther" answers to Ishtar, she "may well be the same as the Amestris of Herodotus". Herodotus makes Amestris the daughter of Otanes; Esther names her father Abihail. Esther 2:15 [11][9]
Artystone, wife of Darius I
James Ussher (1658), who took Ahasuerus to be Darius
Ussher held that Esther was the woman Herodotus calls the virgin Artystone, whom Darius loved above all his wives, though he admits Herodotus makes her a daughter of Cyrus.[25][8]
No: she is known only from Esther
John Urquhart (1915)
Urquhart: "Nothing more is known of her than is recorded in the book which Jewish gratitude has made to bear her name."[20]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say that Esther reigned or ruled in her own right; her writing "with all authority" was with Mordecai, about Purim.
Scripture does not say when or where she died, or whether she had children.
Scripture does not say how long she remained queen.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
From the text"Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle’s daughter": Mordecai, a Benjamite, raised her as his own daughter. Her father was Abihail, Mordecai's uncle. Esther 2:5 Esther 2:7 Esther 2:15
